label: flagship: wins all three exams
result: Final tally (depth-2, strict-value nets, all replay-certified): standard exam 231 of 232 with 0.94 extra moves vs perfect (68% solved perfectly) -- below the pure-subgoal language's proven floor; hard frontier 177 of 218, matching the best solver ever while using ~1-2 fewer moves (47/2 move wins vs the same-budget standard search, fluke ~1 in 200 billion); never-seen boards 188 of 200, +1.47 moves vs perfect on the 137 puzzles with known optima. The win held with two different network pairs and at depths 1 and 2. Caveat: the forward baseline is the original network; a re-tuned forward planner would likely narrow the gap measurement slightly (main FINDINGS 24).
conclusion: The program's flagship planner. Mixing ordinary robot moves into subgoal planning is the single biggest quality change of the entire project; wave-5 question: does training the networks on the search's own chosen slides push further, and does the ceiling break transfer to bigger boards?
note: Search-only change (no training); stochasticity is the search rng only. Gates: unseen moves 31/1 p=1.5e-8; graded moves 30/0 p=1.9e-9.
